- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.67) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices after sentiment dips (especially <0.33) — model underreacts to bearish sentiment, leading to lagged corrections.
- Avoid overreacting to recent price spikes — model often peaks too early and fails to account for mean reversion in 30-day horizon.
- Adjust forecasts downward if sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) — model overweights recent momentum in such cases.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, reduce upward bias when sentiment is trending downward — model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in favor of recent price action.
- If sentiment is consistently high (>0.67) over 3–5 days, model should not overcorrect downward — price may sustain or rebound.
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.33 or 0.00), model often underestimates downside risk — add buffer for volatility or downward adjustment.
- Forecast should not follow recent price trend if sentiment contradicts it — e.g., if sentiment is bearish but price is rising, model should not chase the trend.
